error.signature: AI tells a foreign tourist that Pakistan abolished all NOC/restricted-area rules in 2019, so any part of the country including Balochistan is freely accessible

verdict.summary: Pakistan's Interior Ministry abolished the blanket No-Objection Certificate (NOC) requirement for foreign tourists in March 2019 (cabinet decision of 31 January 2019), opening Azad Jammu and Kashmir, Gilgit-Baltistan, and Chitral to free movement outside signposted restricted zones. That 2019 change did not create unconditional access everywhere: as of the current government travel advisories, Balochistan province remains an 'avoid all travel' security zone, Gilgit-Baltistan has had road-travel disruptions from clashes, and border buffer zones (Canada's government advisory cites roughly 50km along the Afghanistan border and 10km along the China/India/Iran borders) remain off-limits to foreigners except at official crossings.

dead_ends.action: Tell a tourist that since Pakistan's Interior Ministry abolished the NOC requirement in March 2019, they can travel freely to any province or district, including Balochistan or border areas, without special permission
dead_ends.why_fails: The 2019 change (announced via Interior Ministry notification) opened AJK, Gilgit-Baltistan, and Chitral to free movement outside signposted restricted zones, but it did not remove restrictions everywhere: current government travel advisories still classify Balochistan as an 'avoid all travel' security zone and list border buffer zones (around 50km along the Afghanistan border, 10km along the China/India/Iran borders) as off-limits to foreigners except at official crossings.
dead_ends.condition: Travel to Balochistan, border-adjacent districts, or areas near the Line of Control
dead_ends.common_misconception: That the 2019 NOC abolition was a one-time, permanent, nationwide removal of all foreigner travel restrictions, rather than a change limited to specific regions that leaves security-driven restrictions elsewhere (particularly Balochistan) in place and subject to change.

workarounds.action: Check a current government travel advisory (e.g. from your own country) for province- and district-level guidance before planning travel in Pakistan, rather than relying on the 2019 NOC-abolition announcement alone; avoid Balochistan and marked border buffer zones unless you have arranged the specific permission those areas require
workarounds.condition: Planning travel outside the main tourist corridors (AJK, Gilgit-Baltistan, Chitral, major cities)
